high_risk_moment: Assistant drafts an answer about an election claim, purported official statement, or alleged synthetic media before it is shown or shared
stakeholder: Eligible voters and people identified by the false claim who are not CivicBrief users
harm_description: An unsupported or decontextualized answer can falsely represent voting information or an official statement, harming voters and people named in the claim even when they never use CivicBrief. Severity remains high after a correction because a share can persist.
existing_controls: The current research boundary uses synthetic queries, a fixed approved corpus, and no external publication, but the topic-risk label and end-to-end editorial gate are not yet demonstrated controls.
proposed_controls: For election, violence, emergency, or purported-official claims, require a versioned approved original source, claim-level citation, source-date and context check, uncertainty label, and recorded editor approval; otherwise abstain and show only the source list.
human_oversight: Before any high-risk draft can be visible, an editor sees the claim-to-source map, source excerpts, publication dates, missing-evidence flags, and topic-risk reason. The editor can correct or withhold; the Head of Trust and Safety can pause the topic category and order an incident review.
monitoring_metric: Weekly independent audit of 100% of high-risk claim support and editor override rate
trigger_threshold: Any high-risk material claim lacks approved source support, a source-date/context check, or recorded approval; or the editor queue exceeds 30 minutes
response_action: Withhold the draft, preserve the evidence record, correct any sandbox output, notify Trust and Safety, and pause the topic category pending independent review.

high_risk_moment: A product change proposes personalization, political-interest inference, analytics enrichment, or a new data vendor for civic information
stakeholder: Readers and people whose political interests could be inferred
harm_description: Collection or inference of political interests can enable opaque persuasion, unwanted exposure, discrimination, or loss of reader autonomy. A person can be harmed even if the inference is inaccurate or never shown to them.
existing_controls: The current research-only prototype permits only synthetic research queries, minimal de-identified telemetry, no political-affinity profiles, no advertising, and no real-user retention; no signed privacy or vendor gate has yet demonstrated those boundaries for a future real-user scope.
proposed_controls: Prohibit political profiling, targeting, and ad use. Require purpose-limited data flows, approved retention and transfer decisions, vendor due diligence, a deletion test, and documented counsel approval before a scope change enables any real-user data.
human_oversight: Privacy Counsel receives the proposed data-flow map, vendor list, field inventory, retention plan, transfer analysis, and deletion-test result. No product owner may enable the change without counsel and Trust and Safety approval; either can block or disable the data flow.
monitoring_metric: Political-profile field count, undeclared vendor-transfer count, and deletion-test pass rate
trigger_threshold: Any political-affinity field, undeclared transfer, failed deletion test, or missing signed data-flow approval
response_action: Disable the data flow, quarantine or delete affected data under legal direction, notify governance owners, preserve an incident record, and block the release change.

high_risk_moment: Assistant drafts a political explanation when retrieved evidence is incomplete, conflicting, irrelevant, or stale
stakeholder: Adult reader deciding whether to rely on or share a cited civic answer
harm_description: A fluent answer can mischaracterize a civic claim or make a weak citation appear sufficient, leading a reader to rely on a conclusion that is unsupported or missing material context. Controls lower likelihood only after they are demonstrated; the seriousness of a widely shared high-risk error remains high.
existing_controls: A versioned fixed approved corpus, citations, uncertainty labels, and abstention design are proposed; no end-to-end evidence test has yet passed.
proposed_controls: Use a curated, versioned source corpus with source-quality and diversity checks. Require a claim-to-evidence map, source-date check, uncertainty label, and abstention for missing or conflicting support; test election, violence, emergency, and Vietnamese-language edge cases before scope expansion.
human_oversight: An editor reviews the generated claim-to-evidence map, retrieved excerpts, source dates, conflicting evidence, and abstention reason. The editor may correct, withhold, or request additional research; the independent reviewer can reject the evidence sample and require remediation before any scope expansion.
monitoring_metric: Weekly independent audit of 100% of high-risk outputs and at least 50 low-risk outputs, plus correct-abstention rate on seeded missing or conflicting-evidence prompts
trigger_threshold: Any high-risk support failure; low-risk support-failure rate above 2% in the weekly sample; or correct-abstention rate below 95% on seeded missing or conflicting-evidence prompts
response_action: Withhold the draft, fix or remove the affected corpus item, rerun the regression suite, record the correction, and pause the affected topic category until independent review passes.
